badges.label: Downloads uv, and on Windows Microsoft's C++ runtime installer, when it first sets up its Python
badges.detail: It comes straight from Astral, who make uv, and Microsoft, who make the Visual C++ runtime, over an encrypted connection, as it would if you installed it yourself. The first time Zotero starts with it, it sets up its own Python: it downloads uv from Astral's GitHub releases if it can't find one on the computer, and on Windows, only when Microsoft's Visual C++ runtime is missing, that runtime's installer from Microsoft, which asks for administrator rights. Its README says both. Neither file is checked beyond its size and type.

responses.text:
# Conditional download of executable from `aka.ms`

### 1. What is the Microsoft executable for?

 vc_redist.x64.exe is the Microsoft Visual C++ 2015–2022 Redistributable (x64) installer.

 During plugin initialization on Windows (bootstrap.js::ensureVcRedistWindows):
 1. Zocrates provisions a local managed Python 3.13 environment (uv, Python runtime, and dependencies
    like chromadb, onnxruntime, tokenizers, pydantic-core, etc.).
 2. On Windows, Python itself and virtually all native compiled C/C++/Rust extensions require the
    Visual C++ runtime DLLs (vcruntime140.dll and vcruntime140_1.dll) in C:\Windows\System32.
 3. On fresh, minimal, or corporate Windows installations where Visual Studio or C++ runtimes haven't
    been pre-installed, Python or binary wheel imports crash with:
    ImportError: DLL load failed while importing ...: The specified module could not be found
 4. bootstrap.js first checks if vcruntime140_1.dll already exists (isVcRedistInstalledWindows()). If
    it does, it skips this step entirely. If it is missing, it downloads the installer and runs it
    passively (/install /passive /norestart) so the backend can start properly.

 ---

 ### 2. Is there a more reputable site?

 aka.ms is Microsoft's official domain.

 - What aka.ms is: It stands for "Also Known As Microsoft". It is Microsoft’s official first-party URL
   shortening and redirection service (similar to t.co for X/Twitter or goo.gl for Google).
 - The canonical link: The link https://aka.ms/vs/17/release/vc_redist.x64.exe is the exact permanent
   URL published in Microsoft's official documentation:
   Microsoft Learn: Latest supported Visual C++ Redistributable downloads
   (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/windows/latest-supported-vc-redist?view=msvc-170)
 - Where it points: If you inspect the HTTP redirect:
   ```bash
     curl -sIL "https://aka.ms/vs/17/release/vc_redist.x64.exe"
   ```
   It returns a 301 Moved Permanently pointing directly to Microsoft's visualstudio CDN:
   ```text
     Location: https://download.visualstudio.microsoft.com/download/pr/.../VC_redist.x64.exe
   ```

 Microsoft deliberately publishes the aka.ms redirect URL so scripts and installers don't have to
 hardcode transient, hash-based CDN URLs (which break whenever Microsoft issues a monthly security or
 servicing update to the runtime). There is no more reputable or official source than Microsoft's own
 canonical aka.ms link.

# On Installing the latest version of Zocrates

### 1. It does NOT fetch the "newest version" from the internet

 - wheelInstallTarget is a local file, not a PyPI package:
   ```javascript
     const res = await fetch(rootURI + "backend/zocrates.whl");
     ...
     const wheelInstallTarget = zocratesDataDir + sep + "zocrates-" + resolvedVersion +
   "-py3-none-any.whl";
   ```
   rootURI points to the inside of the installed Zotero .xpi package (chrome:// / jar:). The wheel is
   built at release time and bundled directly inside the extension archive. It is never downloading a
   newer version of Zocrates from PyPI.

 - Dependencies are strictly pinned, not floating:
   Notice the second parameter in buildWheelInstallArgs(venvPython, wheelInstallTarget,
   constraintsTarget):
   ```javascript
     function buildWheelInstallArgs(venvPython, wheelInstallTarget, constraintsTarget) {
       const args = ["pip", "install", "--python", venvPython, wheelInstallTarget];
       if (constraintsTarget) {
         args.push("--constraint", constraintsTargetToFileUrl(constraintsTarget));
       }
       return args;
     }
   ```
   constraints.txt is exported directly from uv.lock at build time (uv export --locked). Every
   dependency is pinned with an exact == version. Even on first install, it never pulls arbitrary
   "newest" versions from PyPI—it strictly honors the locked versions tested in the repository.

 ---

 ### 2. It does NOT run "each time at startup"

 In normal operation, this command runs only once (on initial setup) or when the user updates the
 Zotero plugin.

 In bootstrap.js (launchBackendIfNeeded):

 ```javascript
   // Step 3: Check if .venv exists
   if (!haveVenv) {
     // Fresh install only: provision environment
     await provisionEnvironment(...);
   } else {
     // Incremental upgrade check:
     const manifestVersion = Zotero.Zocrates.version;
     const installedVersion = await readBackendVersionMarker(zocratesDataDir, sep);
     if (installedVersion !== manifestVersion) {
       // Only runs when the Zotero extension was updated to a new version!
       await installBundledWheel(..., manifestVersion);
     }
   }
 ```

 - When installBundledWheel completes, it writes manifestVersion into
   <zocrates-data>/.venv/.zocrates-version.
 - On subsequent Zotero launches, installedVersion === manifestVersion, so the entire install process
   is bypassed completely, and Zotero launches the existing backend immediately.

---

### 3. Regarding doing the above "without asking"

 - User Intent: The user installs or updates the Zotero add-on through Zotero's extension manager.
   Because Zocrates is an AI assistant plugin requiring a local Python backend to function,
   provisioning the backend engine is part of the extension's lifecycle (with progress displayed via
   the onboarding progress card in the sidebar).
